creator: stilesai

system.canvas: Single continuous selfie webcam take, warm yellow room, creator centred behind a keyboard. The face is never replaced; graphics are laid over the top of the frame (ceiling and head area) and the footage is punched in or re-framed slightly between sections (head sits higher or lower in the frame).
system.zones: Top 3 to 25 percent of the frame, full width with a small side margin: one white card at a time, covering the ceiling and sometimes the top of the head. Face fills the middle 25 to 70 percent. Captions sit at about 60 to 65 percent height, over the chest. A black-on-white label 'Let your agents doomscroll' sits at the very top for roughly the first 12 seconds.

palette.color: white with a thin black 1px outline, no rounded corners, no shadow
black, plus light grey for 'inactive' or 'forgotten' blocks and mid grey for dimmed ones
tiny green dots and checkmarks, pink message bubble inside the meme screenshot
white text with soft dark shadow, no box

system.type: Cards: tiny uppercase monospace labels (corner tags like MY SAVED FOLDER, THE MEME, SKILL.md) plus a bold neutral grotesque sans for headings and big numbers, regular sans for list items, mono for code. Captions: bold neutral sans, sentence case.
system.captions: 1 to 3 words at a time, lower-middle of the frame, white bold, no highlight on the active word, each phrase hard-swaps to the next in time with speech (about every 0.4 to 0.8 s).
system.rhythm: One card at a time, a new one roughly every 3 to 8 seconds, each tied to a spoken beat (meme, 70 reels, checklist, skill file, You vs Claude, steps, comment prompt). Between cards the top of the frame is bare for about 0.6 s, which lets the face breathe. The cards form a story: 0 to 70 reels, Claude checks off transcripts/frames/captions, grid dims to the few kept, skill file types out, then a You vs Claude comparison.
system.default_transition: Cards leave with a quick fade (about 0.2 to 0.4 s) or a hard cut in under 0.2 s, then there is a short empty gap, then the next card fades in (0.2 to 0.4 s) or pops in. Content inside a card changes by crossfade, line-by-line type-on, or block-by-block fill.
system.restraint: No sound-reactive or camera-shake effects, no colour, no icons or emoji, no animated backgrounds, no text behind the head, no zooms on the cards. Everything is flat black-and-white UI-style cards in a mono and grotesque pairing. The face is never covered by captions. Only one graphic is on screen at once.

graphics.name: meme screenshot card grows
graphics.what: A cropped screenshot of a Claude chat (an agent told to scroll Instagram reels) in a white card with the footer tags THE MEME and CLAUDE, SCROLLING REELS. The strip catches the card changing from a short crop (top of the chat) to a tall crop that covers the top of the head and shows the whole chat.
graphics.trigger: I'm serious. I saw a meme about letting your AI agent doom scroll as a reward
graphics.zone: top 3 to 25 percent, then growing to about 3 to 52 percent of the frame, full width minus margin
graphics.enter: The card was already up before this strip (the 1 fps sheet shows it from about 2 s). Here frame 2 is a translucent crossfade where the head shows through, and frame 3 is a taller card that is still part transparent (head faintly visible through it). Frame 4 is solid. So the crop change is a crossfade of about 0.4 to 0.6 s.
graphics.inside: Content scrolls from the first message to the full conversation (more lines revealed). Footage head position also jumps lower in the same moment, so the footage reframes.
graphics.exit: Next strip shows it crossfading to a shorter crop that highlights one line.
graphics.job: Shows the meme the speaker is describing, so the 'agent doomscrolls' idea is proven rather than told.
graphics.build: Card with fixed width and a tall inner image clipped by overflow hidden. Crossfade the card's content between two crops (or animate card height and image offset) over about 0.5 s. Reframe the video layer with a small scale and y-offset on the same beat.

graphics.name: meme card crossfade to highlighted line
graphics.what: The tall chat card crossfades to a shorter, scrolled crop of the same chat, and a black outline box is drawn round the line 'The dog reel got me ... the other just goes completely limp.'
graphics.trigger: I thought it was the funniest thing I'd ever seen
graphics.enter: Frame 2 is a crossfade (face visible through the card), frame 3 is the shorter card with the line already at the top. The outline box is already present in frame 5, absent in frame 1 and 2 (frame 1 of this strip shows it on the tall card, so the box drew on the tall card before the crossfade).
graphics.inside: A hard black rectangle outline around one line of text, no animation visible between frames.
graphics.exit: Crop scrolls further (next strip) and then the card hard-cuts away.
graphics.job: Points at the joke line so the viewer reads the exact funny bit without a pause.
graphics.build: Overlay an absolutely positioned 2px outlined rectangle over the line, fade or pop on at the line's spoken beat. Move the card to its next crop with a 0.4 s crossfade.

graphics.name: saved folder counter with filling block grid
graphics.what: White card with a big number top-left counting up from 0, the label MY SAVED FOLDER / REELS top-right, and black square blocks that fill in rows beneath it, one block per unit.
graphics.zone: top 3 to 25 percent, full width minus margin
graphics.enter: Previous meme card and the top label vanish in under 0.2 s (frame 2 to 3 is a hard cut to bare ceiling). About 0.4 s of empty top, then the card pops in showing 0 in an empty card (frames 5 and 6). Frame 7 shows 13 and 13 blocks, frame 8 shows 31 and 31 blocks wrapped onto 3 rows.
graphics.inside: Number and block count rise together: 0 to 13 to 31 within 0.4 s, reaching 70 (5 rows of 14) by the next frames. Roughly 70 blocks in under 1 s.
graphics.exit: Fades out (0.2 to 0.4 s) on the next strip, after tag chips TIPS, WORKFLOWS, STUFF I'D COME BACK TO appear under the grid.
graphics.job: Makes '70 saved reels' something you can see and count, and the grid becomes the reusable visual for the reels in later cards.
graphics.build: Card with a number text element and a grid of 70 small black squares set hidden. Tween a counter object 0 to 70 over about 0.8 s, on update set the text and reveal squares up to that index. Add three outlined mono tag chips after the count lands.

graphics.name: grid fades out, Claude checklist fades in
graphics.what: The 70-block counter card fades away and is replaced by a Claude card with a thin progress bar, 'REEL 00 / 70', and three unchecked boxes: Transcripts, Frames, Captions.
graphics.trigger: I handed them to Claude and had to go through every single one
graphics.enter: Old card: frame 2 is a half fade, frame 3 gone, so about 0.2 to 0.4 s fade out. Bare ceiling for about 0.6 s. New card: frame 6 is a half-faded card, frame 7 solid, so about 0.2 to 0.4 s fade in.
graphics.inside: Static at first. The 1 fps sheet shows the progress bar then fills and REEL counter climbs 00 to 70 over about 3.5 s, with Transcripts, Frames, Captions ticking in order as the counter passes thresholds (about 36 and 58).
graphics.exit: Hard cut at about 24 s (next strip).
graphics.job: Shows the agent really working through all 70 reels and what it reads for each one.
graphics.build: Card with title, a counter text, a 3px progress bar and three checkbox rows. Tween a value 0 to 70 over 3.5 s, drive bar width and counter, tick each checkbox when the value passes its threshold.

graphics.name: checklist complete, hard cut to compact reel grid
graphics.what: The Claude progress card finishes (REEL 69 then 70 / 70, all three boxes ticked), vanishes, and a new card appears with a compact 70 REELS block grid in its left third.
graphics.trigger: and the captions. And it didn't just summarize them
graphics.enter: Frames 1 and 2 show the end of the count (bar full). Frame 3 the card is gone (cut in under 0.2 s). Frame 4 the new card is fully there (pop). Grid is a dense 14 by 5 black block field with label 70 REELS.
graphics.inside: Nothing after landing in this strip; in the next strip the blocks go grey except a handful that stay black.
graphics.exit: Next strip: grid dims to light grey with a few black blocks, then a line and arrow draw out to a SKILL.md box, then a hard cut.
graphics.job: Hands the viewer the full set of 70 as one picture, ready for the 'keep only the best' reveal.
graphics.build: Hard cut between two cards (no tween). New card: small grid of 70 black squares plus label. Later tween most squares to light grey and leave about 12 black.

graphics.name: reels grid to SKILL.md arrow, then cut
graphics.what: Grid of reels with most blocks greyed and a few kept in black, caption 'KEPT: WORTH DOING TWICE', an arrow pointing to a SKILL.md document box with grey placeholder lines.
graphics.enter: Frames 1 and 2 show the finished diagram (the build is in the 1 fps sheet: grid dims, an underline extends right, an arrowhead appears, then the SKILL.md box). The card then disappears in under 0.2 s (frame 3 bare).
graphics.inside: Not visible in this strip (static). From the sheet the line draws left to right towards the box over about 1 s.
graphics.exit: Hard cut in under 0.2 s, then bare ceiling for about 1.5 s before the SKILL.md card.
graphics.job: Visualises 'filter to what is worth doing twice, then package it as one skill file'.
graphics.build: Grid of grey squares with about 12 turned black via a staggered fill, a 1px line drawn with scaleX from the grid to a box, arrowhead appears at the end, the box fades in. Hold 1 s then cut.

graphics.name: SKILL.md type-on
graphics.what: A white document card headed SKILL.md and 'ONE OF MY CLAUDE SKILLS' in which the file text types out line by line: front-matter dashes, name: reel-edit-plan, a two-line description. Later a black footer bar reads 'THIS VIDEO WAS EDITED WITH THIS SKILL' and three bullet lines (one continuous still take, word-by-word subtitles, white cards pop in) appear.
graphics.trigger: a skill is basically a saved set of instructions
graphics.zone: top 3 to 22 percent, then growing to about 3 to 25 percent
graphics.enter: Frame 1 bare. Frame 2 is a ghost of the empty card (fade in about 0.2 s). Frame 3 solid with the first dashes.
graphics.inside: Lines appear one per 0.2 s step: --- then name line then description. The description's first half appears, then its second line a frame or two later. Type-on is by whole line or half line, not per character.
graphics.exit: Hard cut on the next beat (sheet: bare ceiling at about 38 s).
graphics.job: Shows what a skill literally is, and the footer proves the reel itself was made by one (a meta payoff).
graphics.build: Card with mono text lines hidden. Reveal each line with a step or fast opacity set at 0.2 to 0.4 s intervals. After the last line, slide in a black footer strip at the bottom of the card.

graphics.name: You vs Claude split card, left panel
graphics.what: A two-column card. The left column is titled 'You' with the sub-label DOOMSCROLLING and 12 black blocks; the right column is empty.
graphics.trigger: And this is where it gets different from us. When you doom scroll
graphics.zone: top 3 to 25 percent, full width, divided vertically in two
graphics.enter: Frame 1 bare. Frame 2 is a ghost of the whole card with the divider and left blocks half visible (fade in about 0.2 s). Frame 3 solid.
graphics.inside: Blocks static here. Per the 1 fps sheet, on the line 'forget all of it by dinner' the left blocks turn light grey and a caption GONE BY DINNER fades in at the bottom of the left column.
graphics.exit: Right panel populates (next strip); the whole card stays.
graphics.job: Sets up a side-by-side contrast of human doomscrolling versus the AI so the next beat reads instantly.
graphics.build: Two-column card, left filled first. Fade the card in over 0.3 s. On the key word tween left block fill from black to light grey and fade in a mono caption.

graphics.name: Claude column pops in and dims to a few kept blocks
graphics.what: The right column of the split card appears titled 'Claude' with the sub-label SCROLLING and 12 black blocks. Over the next frames most of those blocks dim to dark grey and a few stay black.
graphics.trigger: When it scrolls, it keeps what's useful
graphics.zone: right half of the top card, top 3 to 25 percent
graphics.enter: Frame 2 right half is empty, frame 3 right half is complete: pop in under 0.2 s.
graphics.inside: Frame 8 shows the blocks mid-dim: some black, most dark grey. The sheet then shows light grey and a handful of black blocks, and three black pill tags (reel-edit-plan, stilesai-reel-script, reel-diagnosis) stacking below the blocks one every second or so.
graphics.exit: Card fades (0.2 to 0.4 s) and cuts to bare at about 49 s (next strip).
graphics.job: Contrast: the human's grid is all grey (forgotten) while Claude's keeps a few black (kept) and turns them into named skills.
graphics.build: Right column of identical blocks, pop in via opacity set. Then stagger tween most blocks from black to grey over 1 s, leaving about 5 black. Append pill tags one by one with a fast fade and small y offset.

graphics.name: try-it numbered steps card
graphics.what: After the skills card fades out, a new card labelled TRY IT with a numbered list: '1 Go through your saved folder', later '2 Hand it the best ones', '3 Let it scroll'.
graphics.trigger: Go through your saved folder, hand it the best ones, and let it scroll
graphics.zone: top 5 to 17 percent growing to 5 to 20 percent
graphics.enter: Old card: frame 2 faded, frame 3 gone (0.2 to 0.4 s fade). Frame 3 is bare. Frame 4 shows the new card with only line 1: pop in under 0.2 s.
graphics.inside: Lines are added on the spoken words, one per second: line 2 and then line 3 (line 3 comes in lighter, mid fade). The card height stays the same so the list grows into the blank space.
graphics.exit: Next strip: card fades (frame 2 half faded) and is gone by frame 3, about 0.2 to 0.4 s.
graphics.job: Turns the call to action into three clear steps the viewer can follow after the reel.
graphics.build: Card pre-sized for 3 lines. Each line fades in (0.2 s) when its words start. Number in bold, text regular.

graphics.name: comment prompt with input cursor
graphics.what: A card labelled COMMENT with the question 'The one reel you saved and never actually used' in bold above a thin input line with a blinking text cursor, framed like a comment box.
graphics.trigger: what's the one reel you saved and never actually used
graphics.enter: Steps card fades out (frame 2 half, frame 3 gone), bare ceiling for about 0.4 s, then the comment card fades in (frame 5 translucent, frame 6 solid), about 0.2 to 0.4 s.
graphics.inside: A text cursor blinks on the input line (visible in frames 5 and 8, not in 6 and 7). No typing; the question is already in place.
graphics.exit: Not shown, holds to the end.
graphics.job: Invites a comment with an engagement question in a form that looks like the comment box itself.
graphics.build: Card with a mono tag, bold two-line question, a 1px input underline and a 1px wide cursor that toggles opacity every 0.5 s. Fade in 0.3 s.

ideas: Counter plus filling block grid: a big number counts up while one black square appears per unit, so 'I had N of these' reads as a visible pile.
Progress card with ticking checklist: a thin bar fills, a mono counter climbs, and checkboxes tick when the bar passes thresholds, to show an agent working through a task.
Two-column You vs Them card: identical block grids in each column, then one side dims to grey (forgotten) while the other keeps a few black (kept).
Type-on file card: show the real artifact (a skill file) typing out line by line with a black footer bar that says the video itself was made with it.
Single-card-at-a-time story: one flat white card per spoken beat, a short bare gap between cards, and a final comment-box card with a blinking cursor as the call to action.
do_not_copy: The 'Let your agents doomscroll' headline label and the meme screenshot (a specific meme and Claude UI crop)
The skill names reel-edit-plan, stilesai-reel-script and reel-diagnosis and the 'edited with this skill' footer wording
The specific number 70 and the 'worth doing twice' wording
The creator's caption styling and the cap with a number on it
